notes:
Arithmetic Progression (AP)

  • $n$th term: $a_n = a + (n-1)d$.
  • Sum of $n$ terms: $S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d] = \dfrac{n}{2}(a+a_n)$.
  • Arithmetic mean of $a,b$: $A = \dfrac{a+b}{2}$.

Geometric Progression (GP)

  • $n$th term: $a_n = ar^{n-1}$.
  • Sum of $n$ terms: $S_n = \dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}$ for $r\neq1$ (use $\dfrac{a(1-r^n)}{1-r}$ if $r<1$); $S_n = na$ if $r=1$.
  • Sum to infinity (only when $|r|<1$): $S_\infty = \dfrac{a}{1-r}$.
  • Geometric mean of $a,b$: $G = \sqrt{ab}$.

AM-GM inequality

  • For positive numbers, $A \ge G$, with equality only when all the numbers are equal.

Special sums (first $n$ natural numbers)

SumFormula
$\sum n$$\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$
$\sum n^2$$\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}$
$\sum n^3$$\left[\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\right]^2$

Harmonic Progression (HP)

  • A sequence whose reciprocals form an AP. To solve HP problems, invert terms and use AP formulas; there is no direct sum formula.
  • For two positive numbers, $A \ge G \ge H$, and $G^2 = AH$.

Series of odd/even numbers

  • Sum of first $n$ odd numbers $= n^2$. Sum of first $n$ even numbers $= n(n+1)$.

Exam tip

KCET typically sets 2-3 questions from this chapter — usually a direct AP/GP $n$th term or sum, a sum-to-infinity of GP, or an AM/GM insertion problem. Memorise the special sum formulas ($\sum n, \sum n^2, \sum n^3$) since they are often combined with AP/GP questions.
